name: Engineering
question: What does engineering establish about this subject, divided by the quantity whose balance or constitutive closure finishes the predictive model of an artefact?
scqa_question: Which single partition places every engineering claim, procedure and discipline exactly once, with each law cited to its owner?
look_for: EN.O.A1 Force and deformation
EN.O.A2 Mass and momentum
EN.O.A3 Energy and entropy
EN.O.A4 Electromagnetic state
EN.O.A5 Composition and microstructure
find_out: Specification: states function, constraints and acceptance tests before a form is chosen (M1 Represent)

Analysis: turns a Face O model into a number for a stated form (M2 Derive (closed form, dimensional analysis); M5 Compute (FE, FV, circuit solvers, Monte Carlo); M3 Observe (model or prototype test where the closure is unknown))
Synthesis: chooses or generates the form, including optimisation and controller design (M4 Intervene (construct a form); M5 Compute (optimisation))
Making: physical acts on the artefact across its life, from manufacture to retirement (M4 Intervene)
Assurance: checks the artefact against specification (verification), need (validation) and in-service condition (M7 Verify; M3 Observe (metrology, NDT, condition monitoring))
rules_of_thumb: EN.H.1 Factor of safety = capacity / demand, defined only on one failure mode.
EN.H.2 Partial factors and allowable stresses, as calibrated heuristics inside a code's stated scope.
EN.H.4 Miner's linear damage sum, pending sequence effects.
EN.H.5 Rules of thumb: span-to-depth, pipe velocity, approach temperature, current density.
EN.H.7 Risk index = likelihood × consequence, as a screening device.
EN.H.8 TRIZ and quality function deployment, as idea and mapping catalogues.
EN.H.9 Prefer the statically determinate load path you can check by hand.
EN.H.10 Change one thing between prototypes.
collisions: A formula that predicts behaviour lives on Face O. A discretisation, optimiser or test protocol for it lives on Face M.
A law owned by another pyramid is cited, not re-filed: "uses PH.O.A1.5" for Navier–Stokes, Bernoulli, Reynolds number and Hooke.
Maxwell's equations, Faraday's law of induction and the Kirchhoff circuit laws: uses PH.O.A1.2b.
Second law and Carnot limit: uses PH.O.A4.1. First law in engineering form is cited from the same owner.
Arrhenius: uses CH.O.A4.2. Raoult, Nernst and Faraday's laws of electrolysis: uses CH.O.A3.1.
Semiconductor band theory: uses PH.O.A4.4a. EN owns the device curve and drift–diffusion device model.
Shannon–Hartley capacity and the sampling theorem: uses MA.B.C4 (MSC 94A).
Little's law, utilisation ρ = λ/(cμ), Weibull and system reliability: uses MA.O.A5.
LP duality, nonlinear optimisation theory and stability criteria: uses MA.B.C4 (MSC 90, 93).
Error and convergence of FE, FV and Monte Carlo: uses MA.B.C3. Running them is EN.M.B2.
Control theory is a synthesis method (EN.M.B3) on a plant model. It does not add a balance.
A code is a calibrated verification shortcut (EN.M.B5, W12). Using a code outside its scope fails verification.
Physical law and constant (Newton, Navier–Stokes, Maxwell, second law) → PH (PH.O.A1.1, A1.2, A1.3, A1.4b)
Band theory and device physics below the device curve → PH.O.A4.4a
Reaction mechanism, thermochemistry, electrochemical equilibrium → CH.O.A3.1, CH.O.A4.2
Rock and soil genesis, site history, groundwater as earth state → EA.O.A1, EA.O.A4
Theorem: probability, queueing, optimisation, control stability, information theory, numerical error → MA.O.A5, MA.B.C4, MA.B.C3
Software, algorithm, protocol, information state → CS.O.A2.4, CS.M.3
Tissue function, organism in production → BI
Clinical outcome of a device → MD
open: turbulence closure — no general predictive model of turbulent stress for engineering flows; RANS closures are calibrated models (EN.O.A2).
fatigue under variable-amplitude loading — sequence effects lack a general predictive law (EN.O.A1.3.6).
human reliability quantification — current numbers are heuristic (EN.B.C5; uses MS).
Mohr–Coulomb and effective stress EN.O.A1.3.7; alternative EA.O.A1.
information state refused to CS; alternative is a sixth EN balance (v1). Rejected because CS owns the state models and a sixth member is not needed.
operation folded into EN.M.B4 (actions) and EN.M.B5 (in-service integrity); alternative is a separate "operate and sustain" role, which would give six roles and need regrouping.
biomedical and agricultural as substrate rules; alternative is separate bridges (ABET and ANZSRC list biomedical separately).

name: Force and deformation
question: Which idealisations exhaust force-and-deformation models?
look_for: Rigid bodies. Statics: ΣF = 0 and ΣM = 0 when inertia is negligible. Dynamics: ΣF = m a and ΣM = dH/dt about the centre of mass or a fixed point. These laws are Newtonian mechanics (uses PH.O.A1.1). EN owns the free-body reduction and deter
Free-body diagram and static determinacy.
Rigid-body dynamics of mechanisms (linkages, gears, cams).
Lumped vibration models: single- and multi-degree-of-freedom systems with linear springs and viscous damping. Natural frequency ωn = √(k/m) for an undamped linear oscillator.
Slender members. A member whose length greatly exceeds its section is reduced to section resultants plus a kinematic assumption.

Euler–Bernoulli beam. For a prismatic, linear-elastic member with small slopes and plane sections remaining plane and normal: EI d²v/dx² = M(x). With load q positive downward, dM/dx = V and dV/dx = −q (Gere and Goodno, §4.5; sign convention
Timoshenko beam: adds shear deformation and rotary inertia for deep or short beams.
Torsion of a circular shaft. For a linear-elastic, circular or annular, prismatic bar under small twist: T = G J θ / L and τ = T r / J.
Euler column buckling. For an initially straight, slender, linear-elastic, centrally loaded column: Pcr = π² E I / (K L)². Stocky columns leave this formula for a tangent-modulus or code curve.
Kirchhoff–Love plate and Mindlin–Reissner plate. Kirchhoff–Love applies to thin plates with normals staying normal; Mindlin–Reissner admits transverse shear for moderately thick plates.
Thin-walled pressure vessel. For wall thickness much less than radius, under internal pressure p: hoop stress pr/t and longitudinal stress pr/2t.
Deformable continua. The parent theory when section assumptions fail.
Cauchy stress and traction t = σᵀn (uses PH.O.A1.5 for the continuum balance laws).
Isotropic linear elasticity (Hooke). For small strain, a linear, isotropic material: σ = λ tr(ε) I + 2μ ε, with G = E / 2(1+ν). Uses PH.O.A1.5.
Yield criteria: Tresca (maximum shear) and von Mises (distortion energy), for isotropic ductile metals under quasi-static load.
Mohr's circle: principal stresses and maximum shear from the plane-stress transformation.
Linear-elastic fracture mechanics. Under small-scale yielding, K = Y σ √(π a). Mode I, plane-strain failure occurs when K reaches KIc (ASTM E399).

Fatigue life. Basquin (stress-life) and Coffin–Manson (strain-life) relations, fitted per material. Paris law da/dN = C (ΔK)^m holds in region II only; C and m depend on material and R-ratio (Paris and Erdogan 1963).

Geomechanics. Terzaghi effective stress σ′ = σ − u for saturated soil. Mohr–Coulomb strength τ = c′ + σ′ tan φ′ for drained soil and rock joints. CONTESTED: EA.O.A1 (rock and soil as earth materials) is the alternative owner; EN keeps the s
Contact interfaces.

Hertz contact. For two smooth, elastic, non-conforming bodies with frictionless contact and small contact area: contact radius and peak pressure follow from load, curvatures and moduli. CONTESTED: PH.O.A1.5 is the alternative owner.
Coulomb friction: tangential force bounded by μ times normal force, an empirical closure.
Archard wear law: worn volume proportional to load times sliding distance over hardness, with a fitted wear coefficient (UNVERIFIED as to standard notation).
Concepts: stress concentration, Saint-Venant decay, shear centre, slenderness, ductility, redundancy, mechanism.

name: Mass and momentum
question: Which flow domains exhaust mass-and-momentum models in engineering?
look_for: Internal flows.
Bernoulli equation along a streamline, for steady, inviscid, incompressible flow: p/ρ + V²/2 + g z = constant. Uses PH.O.A1.5. A loss term is added, not derived, when the hypotheses fail.
Darcy–Weisbach head loss h_f = f (L/D) V²/2g, where f is the Darcy (Moody) friction factor, four times the Fanning factor.
Colebrook equation and Moody chart for f in fully developed turbulent pipe flow (empirical closure). Minor losses K V²/2g.
Pump and fan matching: head-capacity curve against system curve. Affinity laws hold only between dynamically similar operating points.
Reynolds lubrication equation, for thin, viscous, laminar films with negligible inertia (tribology).
Euler turbomachine equation. For steady flow through a rotor, specific work done on the fluid is w = u₂c_θ2 − u₁c_θ1 (pump or compressor); for a turbine the extracted work is its negative.
Water hammer (Joukowsky surge Δp = ρ a ΔV for instantaneous valve closure in an elastic pipe).

External flows. Drag and lift coefficients; boundary layer; separation as the stall and form-drag mechanism. Reynolds number Re = ρVL/μ = UL/ν (the two forms are equivalent, uses PH.O.A1.5). Flight mechanics and aeroelasticity draw on this
Free-surface flows.
Open-channel specific energy and Froude number Fr = V/√(g h) for a rectangular channel.
Manning equation, an empirical resistance closure for steady, uniform, fully rough open-channel flow.
Ship hydrostatics and stability: buoyancy, metacentric height GM, righting arm, for small heel angles (initial stability).
Hull resistance and seakeeping, with Froude scaling of wave resistance.
Compressible and acoustic flows.
Isentropic nozzle relations for a calorically perfect gas in adiabatic, reversible, quasi-one-dimensional flow. Choked flow when the throat is sonic (M = 1).
Normal-shock relations (Rankine–Hugoniot) for a perfect gas.
Linear acoustics: small-amplitude pressure waves in a quiescent fluid; sound pressure level and transmission loss (noise control).
Porous-medium flows.
Darcy's law q = −(k/μ)∇p for slow, laminar flow through a rigid, saturated porous medium. CONTESTED: EA.O.A4 (groundwater) is the alternative owner.
Ergun equation for pressure drop through a packed bed of particles.
Consolidation (Terzaghi one-dimensional consolidation) for saturated, linear, laterally confined soil.

name: Energy and entropy
question: Which mechanisms exhaust energy-and-entropy models in engineering?
look_for: First-law balances.
Steady open-system first law: Q̇ − Ẇ = Σṁ(h + V²/2 + g z)out − Σṁ(h + V²/2 + g z)in, with heat in and work out positive. The law is owned by physics (uses PH.O.A4.1).
Property closures: ideal-gas model, steam and refrigerant tables (data, W12 and W4).
Cycles as applications: Rankine, Brayton, Otto, Diesel (air-standard idealisations), vapour-compression refrigeration with COP = Q_cold / W.
Second-law limits.
Carnot efficiency 1 − T_c/T_h, the ceiling for a heat engine between two reservoirs at absolute temperatures. Uses PH.O.A4.1.
Exergy: work potential relative to a stated dead state. Irreversibility located per component, not only totalled.
Pinch analysis: minimum approach temperature in a heat-exchanger network.
Heat-transfer rates.
Fourier's law q = −k∇T for an isotropic conductor; plane wall Q = k A ΔT / L at steady state. CONTESTED: PH.O.A4.1 (transport) is the alternative owner.
Newton's law of cooling q = h A (T_s − T_∞), with h from a Nusselt correlation used inside its stated Re and Pr range.

Radiation exchange. Emissive power of a grey surface is ε σ T⁴. Net exchange of a small grey surface with large surroundings is q = ε σ A (T_s⁴ − T_sur⁴), absolute temperatures (Incropera and DeWitt, ch. 1). Enclosures use view factors.
Heat exchangers: LMTD method, or effectiveness–NTU with NTU = U A / C_min.
Fins: added area against a convection boundary, with fin efficiency.

Reacting energy. Heating value and stoichiometry enter the first law as an enthalpy of reaction (uses CH.O.A3.1). Adiabatic flame temperature is the no-heat-loss limit. Fire growth and smoke models for compartments draw on this cell (fire p

name: Electromagnetic state
question: Which reductions of electromagnetic theory exhaust EN models of power and signal?
look_for: Lumped circuits. Valid when the circuit is small compared with the shortest relevant wavelength.
Ohm's law V = I R for a linear resistor; Kirchhoff circuit laws (uses PH.O.A1.2b).
Impedance R, jωL and 1/(jωC), with phasors, for linear circuits in sinusoidal steady state.
Thévenin and Norton equivalents, for linear networks seen from two terminals.

Maximum power transfer. For a linear source with impedance Z_s, load power is maximised when Z_L = Z_s* (complex conjugate). A resistive match applies only to DC or purely resistive sources. A theorem, not a universal design rule.

Linear time-invariant system response: impulse response, transfer function, frequency response. Fourier and Laplace transforms are MA (uses MA.O.A4). State space ẋ = Ax + Bu, y = Cx + Du and G(s) = C(sI − A)⁻¹B + D, for LTI plants.
Sampling theorem. A band-limited signal with no content at or above B is recovered from samples taken faster than 2B per second. Uses MA.B.C4 (MSC 94A).
Concepts: ground and reference, power factor, harmonics, noise figure.
Electromechanical conversion.
Magnetic circuit: Ampère's law with reluctance, for linear core material without saturation.
Ideal transformer V₁/V₂ = N₁/N₂, for zero leakage, zero winding resistance and infinite core permeability.
Machines: torque from current and flux. Synchronous speed n_s = 120 f / p (rpm, p poles). Induction-motor slip.
Power-flow equations for an AC network in balanced steady state (load flow).
Distributed fields.
Transmission line: telegrapher's equations; characteristic impedance; reflection coefficient.
Waveguides and antennas: modes, gain, radiation pattern.
Friis transmission equation for far-field free-space links between matched, polarisation-aligned antennas.
Optical and photonic devices: fibre modes, attenuation, dispersion. Optics as physics (uses PH.O.A1.2c).
Electromagnetic compatibility: coupling paths and shielding; skin effect.
Semiconductor devices.
Diode and MOSFET constitutive curves (e.g., Shockley diode equation for an ideal p–n junction with low injection).
Drift–diffusion device model (uses PH.O.A4.4a for band theory).
Digital abstraction: voltage bands treated as logic levels, with noise margins. Above this abstraction the claim is CS (uses CS.O.A2.4 for the Boolean function).
Power-electronic switching converters: averaged models of buck and boost stages in continuous conduction.

name: Composition and microstructure
question: Which closures exhaust composition-and-microstructure models?
look_for: Reaction rates.
Species balance: accumulation = in − out + generation.
Ideal reactors: batch, continuous stirred tank (perfect mixing), plug flow (no axial mixing). Conversion against residence time; residence-time distribution diagnoses real reactors.
Arrhenius rate constant k = A exp(−E_a/RT), for an elementary or effective rate over a stated temperature range. Uses CH.O.A4.2.
Scale-up limits: mixing and heat removal.
Equilibrium stages.
Raoult's law for ideal liquid mixtures, or a fugacity model when non-ideal (uses CH.O.A3.1).
McCabe–Thiele construction for binary distillation, assuming constant molar overflow.
Two-film theory: interphase flux = K Δc, with an overall coefficient. Rate-based models apply when stage equilibrium fails.
Flowsheet degrees of freedom, recycle and purge.
Microstructure–property relations.
Phase diagram as the equilibrium map (uses CH.O.A3.1 for phase equilibrium).
TTT and CCT diagrams as kinetic maps for steels.
Hall–Petch relation σ_y = σ₀ + k d^(−1/2), for polycrystals over a stated grain-size range (fails at the nanoscale).
Rule of mixtures for composites, as upper (Voigt) and lower (Reuss) bounds, not a point prediction.
Dislocation slip as the mechanism of plastic flow (uses PH.O.A4.4 condensed matter).
Electrochemical cells.
Faraday's laws of electrolysis: mass reacted proportional to charge passed (uses CH.O.A3.1). Applied to corrosion rate and plating.
Nernst equation for the reversible cell potential at stated activities (uses CH.O.A3.1).
Battery and fuel-cell device models: capacity, polarisation curves, state of charge.
Passivation as a kinetic state, not a permanent property.
Neutron balances.
Effective multiplication factor k_eff; criticality at k_eff = 1.
One-group neutron diffusion equation, valid away from boundaries and strong absorbers; transport theory otherwise. Cross-section data uses PH.
Decay heat after shutdown, carried as a source by the energy balance EN.O.A3.1.
Shielding attenuation for a stated source and geometry.
